clue.text: What's the way to produce a greeting?

definitions.text: What's the way to produce a greeting?

parts.words: What's the way to produce a greeting?
parts.note: read as a question about method, but it is itself a formal salutation spoken on meeting someone

explanation.surface: Someone asks how best to greet another person.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal phrase said on being introduced is literally a question asking after one's way of doing things.

clue.text: Dance with one native American

parts.note: to hop is to dance or skip about
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dance performed together with a single indigenous American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Pueblo people of northeastern Arizona.

clue.text: Flee war that's ruined prosperity

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Running away from conflict has wrecked a nation's wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellbeing and good fortune: the state of faring well, a synonym of thriving.

clue.text: Judges one component of this authoritative set

definitions.text: Judges one component of this authoritative set

parts.words: Judges one component of this authoritative set
parts.note: Judges reads as a verb, but it is a book of the Bible, one part of the older scriptural collection

explanation.surface: Someone judges one part of an official collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' looks like a verb; it is the name of a biblical book, and the 'authoritative set' is the scriptural canon containing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew scriptures, including the book of Judges, form the first part of the Christian Bible.

clue.text: Lack nothing on special task

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: O is the round zero figure for nothing
a mission is an assignment with a particular purpose

explanation.surface: Missing nothing while engaged on a particular assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out or absent is a want or gap, a synonym of failing to include.

clue.text: Some children choose to have shower

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some kids decide they want to take a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak thoroughly with water, as a downpour or spray would.

clue.text: Hill collapsed

explanation.surface: A hillside has given way.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern English moorland height; also the past tense of dropping to the ground.

clue.text: The agony of hearing

parts.note: reads like the pain of listening to something awful, but means literal pain in the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: How painful it is to have to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain inside the auditory organ is literally the suffering of the part used for listening.

clue.text: Ache, out of breath rambling

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it
winded means breathless after effort

explanation.surface: Someone aching and panting as they hike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' suggests a walk, matching the breathlessness; here it means talking at great length.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that goes on far too long is wordy and verbose.

clue.text: Greek character was first to water a ram

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to have led is to have been in front
a river is a body of water

explanation.surface: A Greek figure was the first to give a male sheep a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ram' looks like a sheep; it is a machine that drives posts into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that hammers posts into the ground is a kind of pounding device or battering tool.

clue.text: Health food runs into veto

indicators.note: into says the runs letter goes inside the word for veto

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition, a veto
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Wholefood products are hitting a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal husk is eaten for fibre and sold as a dietary supplement.

clue.text: On guard, making sure one has the time?

definitions.text: making sure one has the time?

explanation.definitionFit: Standing sentry on lookout duty; whimsically, retaining one's wristwatch so one can always tell the hour.

clue.text: Cover what's happening in court

explanation.surface: Covering up what goes on in the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A box or protective covering; also a lawsuit heard before a judge.

clue.text: Protected species?

parts.note: reads like an endangered animal, but means an idea or institution placed beyond criticism, like a revered farm animal

explanation.definitionFit: An institution immune from criticism is likened to the bovine animal venerated in Hinduism.

clue.text: Excited atmosphere always in fine place for football

indicators.note: in says the word for always goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a pitch is a field where football is played
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: Football ground always fine, with an excited crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of intense excitement, as at a highly charged sporting fixture.

clue.text: Picky business where many made cross

explanation.definitionFit: A vote is a process of choosing; also an occasion where voters mark a ballot with an X.

clue.text: Organ observed around place

indicators.note: around says the word for observed goes round the place abbreviation

parts.note: seen means observed
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: An organ is noticed in the vicinity of some location.
explanation.definitionFit: An abdominal body part that filters blood, also linked with bad temper.

clue.text: Good free club used by American footballers

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A good free club is offered to players of American football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a sports club; it is the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: The field marked with parallel lines on which American football is played.

clue.text: In a grave situation, so shut up

explanation.surface: Things are serious, so be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To place in a burial vault; also, by extension, to shut away or confine.

clue.text: Act cancelled as a bore

parts.note: a turn is a performance or act on stage
something called off is off

explanation.surface: A performance was scrapped for being dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that puts you off is dull or unappealing.

clue.text: In beast's embrace, it's clear there's no blonde

indicators.note: embrace says the word for clear is held inside the word for beast

parts.note: a brute is a beast
net means clear after deductions, as in net profit

explanation.surface: In the arms of a monster, it's obvious she has no fair hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark hair, the opposite of a fair-haired one.

clue.text: Restart play — or stop it, with towel?

explanation.definitionFit: A football restart from the touchline; also, add 'the towel' and it means to give up.

clue.text: Quiet and secure, with this hedge

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
to rivet is to fasten securely

explanation.surface: A quiet, safe garden enclosed by a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen shrub commonly planted as a garden boundary.

clue.text: Left, having captured knight then queen with mate

indicators.note: having captured says the word for left holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: parted means left or departed
N is the chess notation for knight
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A chess game: a player departs after taking the knight then the queen, then mating.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'mate' look like checkmate; it means a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Paired up with a companion or spouse.

clue.text: Draw back part of lock

indicators.note: back says the word draw is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: Pull back a component of a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge inside a lock that blocks any key without the matching notch.

clue.text: Liberal is unemployed

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous or unrestricted; also not occupied, at leisure.

clue.text: Jog with child across river

indicators.note: across says the word for child stretches round the river letter

parts.note: a tot is a small child
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Running gently with a youngster over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle run, slower than a canter or sprint.

clue.text: Where academics discuss worry, I veto change

indicators.note: change says the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scholar says they will block any change to their work.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of scholarly seclusion, remote from practical everyday concerns.

clue.text: Handle hour at the rear

parts.note: aft means at the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: Dealing with the hour that comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: The grip of a knife, axe or dagger.

clue.text: Very old-fashioned rock group in Wiltshire

definitions.text: Very old-fashioned rock group in Wiltshire

parts.words: Very old-fashioned rock group in Wiltshire
parts.note: reads like a dated band, but the rock is literal standing stones, a prehistoric circle on Salisbury Plain

explanation.surface: A dated band from a rural English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Wiltshire is a county in southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric ring of standing stones on Salisbury Plain, thousands of years old.
